summary: Layer 1B expansion found that the most investable US-listed exposure to this node is not usually labeled as 'education compliance.' The stronger underfollowed lane consists of companies with regulated education-data workflows, student-loan servicing systems, payments, curriculum/testing vendor dependencies, and institutional digital-delivery infrastructure. Obvious reference exposure remains online-learning platforms, but the more interesting second-order candidates are education operators or service providers whose filings reveal recurring spend on LMS, curriculum, testing, software, subscriptions, data systems, and regulated servicing workflows. Several candidates remain hypotheses because customer/vendor evidence must be verified before promotion beyond Layer 1.
